note: Seven adjudicated accidental variants: one capital accent, one comma, and the five words the hand missal sets in display capitals to mark the genuflection. Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero divergence — 189 tokens, letter for letter.

adjudicated.ruling: The typical edition sets the i-form throughout its Ordo — Ioánnem, eius, iunctis — where this edition and Divinum Officium set j, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. Neither is a different word and neither page is wrong; the two orthographies are the two conventions in which the same Latin has been printed for centuries.

House rule (ORTHOGRAPHY.md): accents ARE printed on capitals. Óm-ni-a has three syllables and carries its accent; do omits accents on capitals throughout, and handmissal-eo attests the practice, as at ordinarium.confiteor-sacerdotis w038.

Recorded 2026-08-06, and DISPUTED. This edition prints no comma before the relative, reading qui credunt in nómine ejus as restrictive — it picks out which his are meant and cannot be lifted out of the sentence — following handmissal-eo and the corpus's own rulings at introibo w015 and quid-retribuam w005. But the TYPICAL EDITION prints the comma, and so does Divinum Officium: the authority is against our reading here, and the reading rests on sense rather than on any page. ON THE DISPUTED LIST: an expert should settle whether the edition follows its own sense-reading or the book it is editing.
